title: Can Someone Be Spiritually Gifted and Still Be Lost?
paragraphs: Can Someone Be Spiritually Gifted and Still Be Lost?
There are people who can preach with power…
People who can quote Scripture flawlessly…
and still secretly live in rebellion.

People who move crowds emotionally, cast out demons, prophesy accurately, sing with tears in their eyes, lead churches, fill arenas, trend online, and still hear the most terrifying words ever spoken:
“Depart from Me… I never knew you.”
That verse should shake every soul that has ever confused spiritual activity with spiritual intimacy.
Because there is a terrifying possibility hidden inside modern Christianity:
And most people do not want this conversation.
Because it destroys the illusion that gifting automatically equals godliness.
It exposes the dangerous assumption that charisma is proof of character.
It dismantles the lie that public anointing means private surrender.
And deep down… many people are terrified this might expose them too.
Especially the ones who know how to look spiritually alive.
Especially the ones who learned how to perform Christianity before they ever truly surrendered to Christ.
Especially the ones who built entire identities around ministry while their prayer life quietly died in the dark.
This is not an article for casual readers.
This is for the exhausted worship leader who feels empty after every altar call.
The preacher secretly addicted to sin.
The church kid who learned Christian language but never met Jesus personally.
The believer terrified they are drifting.
The person who knows how to raise hands publicly while privately drowning.
this is for the person who still thinks spiritual gifts are proof of salvation.
The Apostle Paul once wrote words so severe that most modern churches barely talk about them.
“ἐὰν ταῖς γλώσσαις τῶν ἀνθρώπων λαλῶ καὶ τῶν ἀγγέλων… ἀγάπην δὲ μὴ ἔχω, γέγονα χαλκὸς ἠχῶν.”
“If I speak in the tongues of men and angels… but have not love, I am a noisy gong.”
Notice what Paul did not say.
He did not deny the gifts.
He did not deny supernatural experiences.
He did not deny spiritual manifestations.
He said they can exist without true Christlike transformation.
A person can operate in visible spiritual expression while remaining internally untouched.
That should terrify every platform-driven version of Christianity alive today.
And the Greek word used for “knew” in Matthew 7:23 is “ἔγνων” (egnōn), from “γινώσκω” (ginōskō), meaning deep relational knowing, intimate experiential relationship.
Jesus was not condemning people for lacking religious performance.
He was exposing the absence of relationship.
Because Christianity was never supposed to be performance management.
It was supposed to be union with Christ.
And somewhere along the way, many people learned how to imitate spiritual maturity without ever dying to themselves.
Some learned how to preach before learning how to repent.
Some learned how to build ministries before learning how to kneel.
Some learned how to move emotionally during worship without ever allowing God to break their pride.
And slowly… Christianity became image management.
In Matthew 7:22, the people speaking to Him on judgment day sound absolutely convinced they belonged to Him.
Yet Jesus responds by exposing lawlessness.
It means living without submission to God’s authority.
People assume if God uses someone publicly, then God approves everything privately.
In the Old Testament, God used Balaam prophetically while Balaam’s heart remained corrupt.
King Saul prophesied while living in disobedience.
Judas performed ministry alongside the disciples while secretly nurturing betrayal.
And gifts are not the Gospel.
The Gospel is repentance and reconciliation through Jesus Christ.
This is why Galatians 5 becomes so important.
Paul does not say the proof of the Spirit is platform influence.
That is why flesh hates it.
Many people would rather look powerful than become holy.
It costs the version of yourself you carefully built to impress everyone.
But Jesus never died to make people impressive.
He died to make dead people alive.
The Hebrew understanding of the heart goes even deeper.
In Scripture, the Hebrew word for heart is “לֵב” (lev).
It does not merely mean emotions.
It refers to the inner self — the will, mind, desires, intentions, and moral center.
“כִּי הָאָדָם יִרְאֶה לַעֵינַיִם וַיהוָה יִרְאֶה לַלֵּבָב”
“Man looks at the outward appearance, but the LORD looks at the heart.”
He was exposing humanity’s obsession with externals.
And thousands of years later… we still do it.
We know how to create celebrities.
But many churches no longer know how to recognize brokenness.
And brokenness matters deeply to God.
That is what God does not despise.
There are people reading this right now who secretly know something is wrong.
But intimacy with God has been replaced by routine.
And if you are honest… you have become spiritually numb.
One hidden sin at a time.
One ignored conviction at a time.
One private rebellion at a time.
Until eventually you learned how to function spiritually without truly depending on Jesus.
That is one of the most dangerous places a human soul can reach.
And religious routine can imitate relationship.
This is why Jesus constantly confronted the Pharisees.
Because they mastered religion without surrender.
And before modern believers criticize them too quickly…
many Christians today do the exact same thing.
People know Greek word studies but do not forgive others.
Know doctrine but still live in hidden lust.
Know worship lyrics but never crucify pride.
Know church culture but do not know Christ intimately.
And one of the scariest realities is this:
A person can become so skilled at spiritual performance that they fool everyone around them.
“All things are naked and exposed before His eyes.”
Because for the truly surrendered believer, exposure is not destruction.
Jesus does not expose people to humiliate them.
He exposes what is killing them.
The terrifying thing is not conviction.
The terrifying thing is no longer feeling it.
And some people reading this have been asking God for signs while ignoring His conviction.
Asking for gifting while resisting obedience.
But the Kingdom of God does not function that way.
The cross always comes before resurrection.
Jesus never invited people merely to admire Him.
But Christianity without surrender is not biblical Christianity.
And many people today are emotionally attached to Jesus while remaining unwilling to obey Him.
This article is not meant to leave sincere believers in despair.
It is meant to awaken people before it is too late.
Because the same Jesus who warned about false conversion also offered mercy to sinners constantly.
The woman at the well was broken.
The issue was never whether people had a broken past.
The issue was whether they surrendered fully to Christ.
And maybe the deepest tragedy inside modern Christianity is that many people were taught how to look saved instead of how to be transformed.
So they learned behavior modification without heart surrender.
Because pretending to be spiritually alive while dying internally is exhausting.
Tired of trying to maintain an image.
Tired of wondering if God still wants you.
Jesus did not die for the fake version of you.
He died for the real you.
The version of you nobody else fully sees.
And the invitation of the Gospel has never been “clean yourself first.”
The enemy wants people trapped in one of two extremes:
But the Holy Spirit leads people into truth.
If conviction is hitting you right now, that is not proof God abandoned you.
It may actually be proof He is still calling you.
Because dead hearts do not usually care about repentance.
And if your soul feels exposed while reading this…
There is still mercy at the cross.
Still cleansing through the blood of Jesus Christ.
But stop confusing gifting with intimacy.
Stop confusing church activity with surrender.
And stop assuming emotional experiences automatically equal spiritual rebirth.
Jesus did not say many would be rejected because they lacked gifts.
And one day… every hidden thing will be revealed.
Nothing will matter more in that moment than whether you truly knew Christ…
and whether Christ truly knew you.
And maybe that reality hits harder because deep down…
you already knew this article was about more than other people.
One day every stage light will die… but eternity will still remember who truly belonged to Jesus.
